questions.question: What HTTP verbs and status codes does a Rails API use?
questions.title: HTTP Verbs and Status Codes in Rails
questions.direct_answer: The verbs: GET (read, no side effects — index/show), POST (create — create), PUT/PATCH (update — update; PATCH for partial), DELETE (remove — destroy). Rails maps them to controller actions by REST convention. The status codes: 200 OK (success), 201 Created (after POST creates a resource), 204 No Content (after DELETE, no body), 400 Bad Request (client error), 401 Unauthorized (not logged in), 403 Forbidden (logged in but not allowed), 404 Not Found, 422 Unprocessable Entity (validation failure in Rails), 500 Server Error. You set a status with render json: x, status: :created. Using the right verb and status is the contract a well-behaved API keeps.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know the verbs (GET/POST/PUT-PATCH/DELETE) map to REST actions, and the common status codes (200/201/204/400/401/403/404/422/500).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Returning 200 for a create (use 201), or 404 for a validation failure (use 422 in Rails).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Verbs: GET/POST/PUT-PATCH/DELETE map to index/create/update/destroy. Status: 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400/401/403/404, 422 (validation), 500.

sections.title: The API's Contract
sections.content: The verbs: GET to read with no side effects (index, show), POST to create (create), PUT or PATCH to update (update; PATCH for partial), DELETE to remove (destroy). Rails maps them to controller actions by REST convention. The status codes: 200 OK for success, 201 Created after a POST creates a resource, 204 No Content after DELETE with no body, 400 Bad Request for a client error, 401 Unauthorized when not logged in, 403 Forbidden when logged in but not allowed, 404 Not Found, 422 Unprocessable Entity for a validation failure in Rails, and 500 for a server error. You set a status with render json x, status created. Using the right verb and status is the contract a well-behaved API keeps.

sections.title: Verbs and Codes
sections.content:
GET/POST/PUT-PATCH/DELETE; 200/201/204/400/401/403/404/422/500.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  G[GET: index/show] --> P[POST: create -> 201]
  P --> U[PATCH: update -> 200]
  U --> D[DELETE: destroy -> 204]
```

sections.title: Verbs and status in Rails
sections.content:
```ruby
module Api
  class PostsController < ApplicationController
    # GET /api/posts      -> index  (200)
    def index; render json: Post.all; end

    # GET /api/posts/:id  -> show   (200, or 404)
    def show; render json: Post.find(params[:id]); end

    # POST /api/posts     -> create (201)
    def create
      post = Post.create!(post_params)
      render json: post, status: :created   # 201
    end

    # PATCH /api/posts/:id -> update (200, or 422 on validation fail)
    def update
      post = Post.find(params[:id])
      post.update!(post_params)
      render json: post                      # 200
    end

    # DELETE /api/posts/:id -> destroy (204, no body)
    def destroy
      Post.find(params[:id]).destroy
      head :no_content                      # 204
    end
  end
end
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Returning 200 for a create — use 201 Created.
404 for a validation failure — Rails uses 422 Unprocessable Entity.
Using PUT for a partial update — PATCH is the convention for partials.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Verbs: GET (read), POST (create), PUT/PATCH (update; PATCH for partial), DELETE (remove).
Rails maps verbs to REST actions: index/show/create/update/destroy.
Status codes: 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 401/403/404, 422 (validation), 500.
Set a status with render json: x, status: :created; head :no_content for 204.
422 (not 404) is Rails' convention for a validation failure.

The status codes: 200 OK for success, 201 Created after a POST creates a resource, 204 No Content after DELETE with no body, 400 Bad Request for a client error, 401 Unauthorized when not logged in, 403 Forbidden when logged in but not allowed, 404 Not Found, 422 Unprocessable Entity for a validation failure in Rails, and 500 for a server error. A common mistake is returning 200 for a create, when you should use 201, and 404 for a validation failure, when Rails uses 422.
